gates.evidence: The proposal targets a 'Services Tab' surface and offers a standard feature trial, which is inherently SFW and age-appropriate.
The reward is a 30-minute entitlement trial; there are no incentives for clicks, installs, or ratings, and no cash rewards.
The proposal uses standard 'Maybe later' fallback logic; there is no hostage framing, confirmshaming, or nagging.
The offer requires a proactive tap on the 'Play to try' CTA card located on the Services Tab.
The card copy states: 'Play a 15-second game to try 30 minutes of Upgrade to Luzia+' prior to opt-in.
The UI provides a clear 'No thanks' decline option that leaves the user on the Services Tab with no penalty.
The offer appears as a persistent card on the navigation hub (Services Tab), never mid-chat or mid-generation.
Eligibility is strictly limited to guests who have declined account creation; existing subscribers are excluded.

scores.evidence: The offer appears exactly when the user has expressed a need but is not yet ready to commit to account creation, which is the definition of a fallback opportunity.
The offer is non-interruptive (hub-based) and preserves the user's current session state entirely.
The trial is strictly time-boxed (30 mins), limited to 1x/day, and only offered to decliners, keeping the permanent premium tier unique.
As an entitlement-based unlock (no cost per message incurred by the sample), the COGS is near zero, making this highly profitable given US revenue rates.
The Services Tab (s06) is a high-traffic navigation tab in the core loop (f5, m18).
Maps directly to SIM-RWD logic, but referenced an invalid screen ID (s99) instead of the actual screen (s06).
References Luzia nouns such as 'Luzia+' (r1), 'Services Tab' (s06), and the Create Account Sheet (s07).
The offer is explicitly capped at once per day, preventing nagging.
Includes a clearly defined holdout (10%) and success metrics (conversion vs retention).
